headline: Semis and Homebuilders Drag Wednesday Lower as Earnings Splits Define the Session
body_html:
Wednesday's session closed on a decidedly defensive note, with decliners outpacing advancers 349 to 167 across the 519-name universe. The dominant theme was a punishing divergence in earnings reactions: companies that missed or warned were treated harshly, while the handful that cleared the bar surged dramatically. The Federal Reserve held rates steady, as widely expected, but its decision did little to lift sentiment as investors turned their attention to what major technology firms will signal about artificial-intelligence spending in forthcoming reports.

Sector rotation told the story plainly. Energy led all groups, advancing 0.83%, followed by Software at 0.75%, while Healthcare and Consumer each eked out modest gains of 0.22%. The damage was concentrated lower down: Semiconductors cratered 4.96%, Industrials fell 2.97%, Homebuilders shed 2.76%, and Materials dropped 2.38%—a broad sweep of cyclical and rate-sensitive names that found no refuge.

The session's standout mover was Verra Mobility, which surged 22.01% on what appeared to be a strong earnings catalyst, joined closely by Manhattan Associates, up 21.32%, in a reminder that selective results-driven gains are alive even in a down tape. Lennox International, off nearly 21%, was the mirror image on the downside.

briefs.headline: Fed Holds Steady, but AI Spending Scrutiny Takes Center Stage
briefs.body: The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at its July meeting, drawing five key takeaways from officials' commentary. With that decision now in the rearview, investors are pivoting quickly to assess what major technology platforms will disclose about their artificial-intelligence capital expenditure commitments in upcoming quarterly calls, a figure seen as a barometer for the broader AI infrastructure buildout.

briefs.headline: Hims & Hers Tumbles as FTC Moves on Data and Billing Allegations
briefs.body: Shares of Hims & Hers Health fell 14.73% Wednesday after the Federal Trade Commission filed suit against the telehealth company over alleged improper data and billing practices. The stock had already slid roughly 10% intraday before the final close extended losses further, making it one of the session's sharpest single-stock declines tied directly to a regulatory headline.

briefs.headline: Verra Mobility's 22% Surge Headlines Earnings-Driven Movers
briefs.body: Verra Mobility posted the session's largest percentage gain, jumping 22.01%, as investors rewarded the Industrials-Mobility company following what the market read as a convincingly positive quarterly result. Manhattan Associates, a supply-chain software specialist, was a near match, rising 21.32% and reinforcing the view that earnings execution—not macro—is the fulcrum for individual names this reporting season.

briefs.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Lift Energy Even as Broader Market Weakens
briefs.body: Energy was the session's top-performing sector, gaining 0.83%, amid fresh geopolitical friction in the Middle East and North Africa. A reported drone strike on a gas storage tanker near Egypt's Mediterranean port, combined with new U.S. sanctions targeting Iran-linked insurers and shipping vessels, kept supply-risk premiums elevated and offered commodity-exposed equities a degree of insulation from the wider selloff.

briefs.headline: Lennox, Watsco, Masco Signal Trouble Across the HVAC and Building-Products Chain
briefs.body: Three names tied to residential and commercial building systems suffered severe declines Wednesday: Lennox International shed 20.97%, Watsco dropped 12.92%, and Masco fell 11.09%. The synchronized pressure across HVAC distributors and building-products manufacturers reinforced the weak Homebuilders and Industrials sector readings, suggesting that rate-sensitive demand expectations are being marked down materially by the market.

briefs.headline: Humana Holds Its Ground as Healthcare Earnings Picture Stays Mixed
briefs.body: Managed-care operator Humana topped quarterly consensus estimates and reiterated its full-year profit guidance, citing medical costs that remained within projected ranges. The result offered a constructive data point for the Healthcare sector, which managed a 0.22% gain on the session even as subsectors including telehealth and diagnostics traded in opposite directions on their own company-specific news.
